title: Work done by a gas: W = P × ΔV
summary: A gas expanding against constant pressure does work equal to the pressure times the change in volume.
alt: A gas pushing a piston outward at constant pressure, with a shaded rectangle on a P–V graph showing the work as an area.

gas.label: Gas molecules
gas.text: The molecules of the gas (colour = speed: blue slow, red fast).

me.label: Live reading
me.text: What the simulated gas shows right now.

work.label: Work
work.text: Work done by (or on) the gas.

steps.title: A gas at constant pressure
steps.text: The gas pushes on a piston with a steady pressure \( P = 200 \) kPa (the red arrow). It starts with a volume of 2 L.

steps.title: The gas expands
steps.text: The gas heats up and pushes the piston out. The piston moves a distance \( d \). The force of the gas is \( F = P \times A \), where \( A \) is the piston area.

steps.title: Force × distance
steps.text: Work is force times distance: \( W = F \times d = (P A)\,d = P\,(A d) \). But \( A d \) is the **change in volume** \( \Delta V \). So \( W = P \Delta V \).

steps.title: Work is the area
steps.text: On the P–V graph the work is the **area of the rectangle** under the constant-pressure line: height P, width ΔV. Here \( W = 200 \times 2 = {{W|0}} \) J.

steps.title: Compression: work done on the gas
steps.text: Push the piston back in. The volume **decreases**, so \( \Delta V \) is negative and the work done **by** the gas is negative: the surroundings do work **on** the gas.

formulas.title: Work done by a gas (constant P)
formulas.text: P in pascal, V in m³, W in joule. W > 0 when the gas expands, W < 0 when it is compressed.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A gas at a constant pressure of **200 kPa** expands from **2 L** to **5 L**. How much work does it do, in joules? (1 L = 10⁻³ m³)

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A gas at **100 kPa** is compressed from **4 L** to **1 L**. What is the work done **by** the gas (joules)? Use a negative sign if it is done on the gas.
challenges.explain: \( W = 1\times10^5 \times (-3\times10^{-3}) = -300 \) J: the surroundings do 300 J of work on the gas.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: On a P–V graph at constant pressure, the work done by the gas equals:
challenges.explain: W = P ΔV is the area of the rectangle under the line.

takeaways: \( W = P\Delta V \) at constant pressure: force on the piston times the distance it moves.
Expansion: **W > 0** (gas does work). Compression: **W < 0** (work is done on the gas).
On a P–V graph, **work = area** under the curve.

notes.title: Connects to
notes.text: If the pressure is **not** constant, the work is still the area under the P–V curve (see *Work is the area under P–V*). The work is part of the energy bookkeeping of the **first law**.
